summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored documents from Anguilla (Economic Residence Act and Regulations, two Executive Council minutes, the 2018 ARBI presentation), Argentina (DNU 366/2025, Decrees 524/2025, 285/2026 and 616/2010, Ley 27802), Saudi Arabia (Premium Residency Law in English, three Umm al-Qura texts of the 2024 amendment, an SPA news item) and Sierra Leone (two amending citizenship laws, Immigration Department policy, notice and press release). None has statistics apart from Argentina's visa-free claim; the work is rules: the full Anguilla fee schedule and Act rules, Saudi law time limits and the repealed age-21 rule, Argentina's decision deadline. Sierra Leone has no programme: its laws and policy carry no investment route.

events.title: Executive Council sets retroactive fast-track valuation tiers for the planned residency programme
events.description: Reviewing the proposed Permanent Residency by Investment Programme, Executive Council agreed that the minimum property valuation for the Retroactive Fast Track Phase be US$750,000 if the purchase was less than 2 years ago, US$600,000 if 2-5 years ago and US$500,000 if over 5 years ago, and that dependent children up to 26 in full-time study and financially dependent be eligible. These tiers were later written into the Anguilla Economic Residence Act.
events.quote: if the purchase occurred between 2-5 years ago, the valuation threshold should be a minimum of US$600,000

events.title: Executive Council approves a retroactive-track residence-by-investment application
events.description: Executive Council approved, under s. 10(2) of the Anguilla Economic Residence Act, the application of a principal applicant on the retroactive track (East End property owned since 31 August 2018, valued above the US$750,000 threshold), after noting the due diligence outcome, and asked that the applicant fulfil any requirements within 60 days. Shows the retroactive route in use in late 2022; the minutes give no counts.
events.quote: approved the application pursuant to section 10(2) of the Anguilla Economic Residence Act

events.title: Ministry of Finance presents the proposed Anguilla Residency by Investment (ARBI) design
events.description: Public information session on a tentative design: Phase 1, a Retroactive Fast Track period for owners of property bought before launch (tentatively Q4 2018, open at least 6 months, 30-day turnaround), then Phase 2, the full programme (tentatively Q1 2019). Proposed routes: real estate of at least US$750,000 for a family of up to 4 (US$100,000 more per extra member; no resale within 5 years), Capital Development Fund US$150,000, and a tax residency route still being explored. Proposed fees (full programme): processing US$3,000 per family of up to 4 and US$500 per extra member, due diligence US$7,500 per adult and US$3,000 per child under 18, permit fee (real estate only) US$10,000 single, US$20,000 family of 4, US$5,000 per extra member. Retroactive period: processing US$2,000 and US$250, due diligence US$500 per adult and US$0 per child, permit US$5,000 single, US$10,000 family of 4, US$1,000 per extra member. The existing non-investment route: permanent residence after 10 consecutive years of at least 6 months a year, permit EC$1,000 renewable annually. Several of these amounts differ from those later enacted (e.g. due diligence for children US$2,500 and for retroactive adults US$1,000 in the 2020 Regulations). Applications only through authorised local agents. Naturalisation as a BOTC needs 9 months' residence a year for 5 consecutive years.
events.location: PDF pp. 9-21 (slides 'Launch of Program' to 'Role of Authorized Local Agents')

events.title: Citizenship-by-investment agency must publish investments received each year
events.description: Among the powers given to the new Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión (new art. 6 ter of Law 346): implement CBI programmes, publish annually the investments received by them, receive and evaluate applications with reports from the Migration Directorate, UIF and others, and send a reasoned recommendation to the Migration Directorate. Its Executive Director (rank of Under-Secretary) must also prepare and publish an annual report (art. 6 quáter g). Funded from the Ministry of Economy budget (art. 46).
events.location: Arts. 40-42 (new arts. 6 bis, 6 ter, 6 quáter of Law 346), art. 46
events.quote: 2°. Publicar anualmente las inversiones recibidas por los programas de ciudadanía por inversión.

ledger.contains: Anguilla Economic Residence Act, revised edition as at 31 Dec 2022 (20 PDF pages; consolidates Act 15/2019, 21/2020, 35/2020). Creates residence by investment (RBI: Capital Development Fund contribution or approved real estate, plus a retroactive route for property bought before 31 May 2019 at US$750,000/600,000/500,000 by purchase period) and residence for tax purposes (RTP: 5 years of annual lump-sum tax, approved real estate, 45 days a year), combination option, application procedure, review committees, Executive Council decision, grounds for refusal and revocation (incl. resale within 5 years), authorised agents (one-year licence). Amounts for the main routes are only 'prescribed' (set in the Regulations). No statistics. Rules and the two amending Acts now extracted; the US$750,000 retroactive tier and the 2019 launch were already in the data.

Anguilla Economic Residence Regulations, revised edition as at 31 Dec 2022 (8 PDF pages; revises R.A. 99/2020, in force 4 Dec 2020): application through an authorised agent, payment of fees (due diligence once when applying for both RBI and RTP), replacement permits, agent applications, and the Schedule of fees and amounts for the real estate route, the retroactive real estate route (property bought on or before 31 May 2019), the Capital Development Fund route and the tax residence programme. No statistics. All schedule amounts now extracted (four were already in the data: US$750,000 real estate, US$150,000 fund, US$10,000 single permit fee, US$75,000 annual tax payment).

Minutes of the 175th Executive Council meeting, 7 Feb 2019 (8 pp.). Programme items: Ex Min 19/71 on the proposed Permanent Residency by Investment Programme (Retroactive Fast Track Phase deadline extended to 30 June 2019; valuation tiers US$750,000 / 600,000 / 500,000 by time since purchase; dependants under 26 in full-time study; request to put the scheme in primary legislation) and Ex Min 19/72 authorising the Governor to grant one Permit of Permanent Residence via Investment under s. 24(1) of the Immigration and Passport Act and the Permanent Residence Permit (Amendment) Regulations 2018 (a single case, no amount; not recorded as a count). The rest is out of scope: 2019 capital and recurrent budget figures (no programme line), ports, Airbnb tax, planning appeals, training, a national funeral, travel.

Minutes of the 116th Executive Council meeting, 8 Dec 2022 (5 pp.). Programme items: Ex Min 22/388 approving draft Capital Development Fund Regulations 2022 because the US$150,000 fund route of the Economic Residence Act had been inoperable without the fund (already in the data as an event); Ex Min 22/389 approving one retroactive-track RBI application (property valued above US$750,000; a single case, recorded as an event, not as a count). Out of scope: work permit refusals (6 persons, EC$8,800.50 lost revenue).

Ministry of Finance slide presentation for the ARBI public information session, 23 Aug 2018 (22 slides), marked tentative and confidential: purpose, benefits, BOTC naturalisation requirement (9 months a year for 5 years), residency vs citizenship, two-phase launch plan, the existing 10-year residence route (EC$1,000 annual permit), proposed real estate (US$750,000, +US$100,000 per extra member, 5-year hold), Capital Development Fund (US$150,000) and tax residency routes, due diligence firms, revocation, proposed fee schedules for the full programme and the retroactive fast-track period, role of agents. No statistics. Because this is a proposal that was never in force in this form, its amounts are recorded in one event description rather than as programme terms (the enacted amounts are in the 2020 Regulations).

Boletín Oficial page for Decreto 285/2026 (dated 27 Apr 2026, published 28 Apr 2026): two articles appointing, ad honorem and from 22 Apr 2026, the Executive Director of the Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión (Ministry of Economy). No amounts or statistics. The appointment is already in the data as an event; nothing else to add.

Boletín Oficial page for Decreto 524/2025 (dated 30 Jul 2025, published and in force 31 Jul 2025): procedure for citizenship-by-investment applications. Applications go to the Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión, which judges whether the investment is 'relevant' (as the Ministry of Economy will define), asks security, financial-intelligence (UIF), criminal record, RENAPER and SIDE bodies for reports, and sends a recommendation to the National Migration Directorate, which decides within 30 working days; ARCA to issue tax IDs (CUIT) to new citizens; the Agency may issue further rules. No investment amount or statistics. Procedure already in the data as an event; the 30-day decision limit added.

Boletín Oficial page for DNU 366/2025 (28 May 2025, published and in force 29 May 2025): a broad reform of the Migration Law 25.871 (permanent residence conditions, impediments, expulsions, fees for health care and university studies for non-residents, education), the Higher Education and National Education laws, and the Citizenship Law 346. Programme content (Title III, arts. 37-43, and arts. 45-46): naturalisation for a 'relevant investment' regardless of residence, defined by the Ministry of Economy; creation, powers and director of the Agencia de Programas de Ciudadanía por Inversión (incl. annual publication of investments received); naturalisation moved from the courts to the Migration Directorate. Recitals give the passport's visa-free access (more than 170 countries) and US deportation figures (out of scope). Ordinary naturalisation becomes 2 years' continuous residence with no trips abroad, age 18+ (general naturalisation, not the programme). No investment amount. The creating provision was already an event; added the visa-free figure and the annual-publication duty.

Boletín Oficial page for Ley 27802, Ley de Modernización Laboral (published 6 Mar 2026): labour contract and collective bargaining reform, a medium-investment incentive regime (RIMI) and tax changes (VAT, income tax). Programme content is only art. 194 (new last paragraphs of art. 116 of the Income Tax Law): people naturalised for a relevant investment do not become tax residents merely by naturalisation and are treated as foreign nationals for art. 116(b), unless already permanent residents. No amounts or statistics about the programme; that article is already in the data as an event. Everything else is out of scope.

InfoLEG text of Decreto 616/2010 (3 May 2010), the full regulation of Migration Law 25.871 (entry, residence categories, documents, impediments, expulsion, procedures). Programme content is art. 23(d) of the Annex: the investor subcategory of temporary residence requires a productive, commercial or service investment of interest to the country of at least ARS 1,500,000, proof of the origin and lawful source of funds entering through authorised banks, a non-binding opinion of the Ministry of Industry and Tourism on the project (nature, legal viability, economic sustainability), and a binding deadline for making the investment set by the Migration Directorate (no number of days given). The rentista (passive income) subcategory sets no amount. Both the ARS 1,500,000 term and the launch event are already in the data; no statistics. Everything else is general migration regulation, out of scope.

English translation (4 pp., Premium Residency Center) of the Premium Residency Permit Law as amended in 1445H: definitions; rights of holders (residence with family, visas for relatives, domestic workers, property ownership outside Mecca, Medina and border areas, usufruct in Mecca and Medina up to 99 years, private-sector work, visa-free exit and entry, commerce); two types (permanent, fixed-term) with products and fees approved by the Council of Economic and Development Affairs (no amounts in the law); requirements (passport, solvency, clean record, medical report under 6 months; minimum age repealed); 30 days to pay fees and get health insurance; cancellation grounds (crime punishable by 60+ days or SAR 100,000+ fine, deportation, false information); Arts. 8, 10(1) and 11(2) shown as repealed. No fee amounts or statistics. Rules with numbers now extracted; the amendment itself is already an event from the Umm al-Qura text.

Saudi Press Agency news item (Riyadh, 10 Jan 2024): the Premium Residency Center chairman announces five new premium residency products (exceptional competence, talent, business investor, entrepreneur, property owner), who each is for, and general benefits (business, property ownership and usufruct, work permits for holder and family). It prints no amounts, fees or counts; the launch is already in the data as an event.

Umm al-Qura page for Council of Ministers Resolution No. 437 of 6/6/1445H (published 10 Jan 2024) approving the amendment of the Premium Residency Law (Royal Decree M/106 of 10/9/1440H), listing the papers considered (Premium Residency Center letter of 10/6/1443H, Experts Commission memos, CEDA minutes of 5/4/1445H, Shura Council resolution 354/46, General Committee recommendation) and attaching a draft royal decree. No amounts or statistics; the 2019 law's date is already in the data as an event from this page, and the amendment's content is extracted from sau-uqn-prl-amendment-2024.

Umm al-Qura text of the amendment to the Premium Residency Law (published 10 Jan 2024), 12 items: new definition of family (dependants: spouses, children, parents); visa-free exit and return; two types (permanent, fixed-term) with products and fees proposed by the Board and approved by the Council of Economic and Development Affairs; repeal of the minimum age of 21; decision by the Center's head; payment of the CEDA-approved fee; repeal of Art. 8 (holder treated as resident for tax purposes), Art. 10(1) and Art. 11(2) (no right to Saudi citizenship). No fee amounts or statistics. The amendment is already an event; the repealed age-21 rule added as a dated term.

Umm al-Qura page for Royal Decree No. M/84 of 11/6/1445H (published 10 Jan 2024): approves the amendment of the Premium Residency Law (Royal Decree M/106 of 10/9/1440H) in the attached form, citing Shura Council resolution 354/46 of 26/2/1445H and Council of Ministers resolution 437 of 6/6/1445H. No amounts or statistics; the amendment is already in the data as an event (from sau-uqn-prl-amendment-2024).

Sierra Leone Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2006, Act No. 11 (3 pp., Gazette 28 Dec 2006): dual citizenship, citizenship by birth through the mother, definition of a person of Negro African descent, new conditions for naturalisation certificates (s. 9: full age, oath, declaration on residence and employment, prescribed fees, no amount), deprivation of citizenship of naturalised persons and an appeal committee, resumption of citizenship, repeal of ss. 6, 11, 23. No investment route and no numbers about any programme; Sierra Leone has no programme in the dataset. Used as context only.

Bill for the Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2017 (1 p., Gazette 22 Jun 2017): replaces s. 5 of the Citizenship Act 1973 so citizenship by descent passes through the father or the mother, with its memorandum of objects. Nothing on investors or naturalisation by investment; no numbers. Context only.

Sierra Leone Immigration Department public notice (1 p., scanned; read by OCR at 300 dpi): ordinary naturalisation resumes from 1 October 2024; list of documents (passport, 3 photos, certificates, evidence of residence for the last 8 years, travel in and out for the last 5 years, current employment or business, earnings for the last 5 years). No investment route and no programme numbers. The resumption and 8-year requirement are already in the data as a context event; nothing else in scope.

Sierra Leone Immigration Department 'Policy Guidance on Sierra Leone Citizenship Laws' (5 pp., undated, c. 2020): summary of the Citizenship Acts 1973, 1976, 2006 and 2017 and passport policy: citizenship by birth and descent, naturalisation (age 21, 8 years' residence for persons of Negro African descent, 15 years for others), naturalisation by marriage, conditions for certificates, passport approvals for naturalised citizens, dual citizenship, resumption of citizenship. Notes that naturalisation applications are few and the process has at times been suspended (no numbers). No investment route and no programme numbers; Sierra Leone has no programme in the dataset. Context only.

Two-page press release in the name of the Sierra Leone Immigration Department, 2 Jan 2025 (copy distributed via an industry site; authorised 'SLID / CIO / 23-12-24'): announces 'new arrangements' to naturalise high-net-worth foreign investors and people of Sierra Leonean heritage, with quotes from the Chief Immigration Officer; lists the department's achievements (MoU with the Belgian Immigration Office, Dec 2023; new uniforms, Nov 2024; launch of the GO-FOR-GOLD residency programme, Dec 2024) and passport reforms. No amounts, legal basis or counts. Both the announcement and the GO-FOR-GOLD launch are already in the data as events; nothing else in scope.
